`branch` is a bundled Consuelo OS skill. Aligns a large engineering effort before implementation, audits hidden dependencies, builds a dependency graph, and freezes branch-sized PR contracts with explicit parallel lanes.

## When to use it

Invoke when Ko asks to decompose or branch a large project into multiple PRs, chats, or agents; plan an epic across sequential and parallel workstreams; decide what can run in parallel; freeze a technical branch stack; or execute an established 'Branch N approved, go' plan. Do not invoke for ordinary Git branch commands or a single already-scoped repo task.

Typical requests include:

- “Break this migration into PRs and tell me what can run in parallel.”
- “Branch 3 approved, go.”

## Enable it

```bash
consuelo add skill branch
```

Run `consuelo add skill` without a name to choose from the skills that are not currently selected. Remove it with:

```bash
consuelo remove skill branch
```

## What the agent loads

The installed metadata points to `skills/branch/SKILL.md` in the immutable OS runtime. The compact steering catalog advertises the active skill by name and description; the full `SKILL.md` body is loaded only when the workflow applies.

Metadata for this skill currently declares permission `guidance` and `requiresApproval: no`. Those fields describe the skill contract; individual tools called by the skill still enforce their own authorization and safety rules.

## Boundary

Use Branch Planner to decide the work units. Use Task Workflow to execute one approved work unit. Do not invoke it for an ordinary Git branch or an already-scoped single task.

## Verify

After enabling it, confirm `~/Consuelo/Skills/branch/SKILL.md` exists and that `branch` appears in `<CONSUELO_HOME>/components/installed-skills.json`. A newly bootstrapped agent should then see `branch` in the Installed skills portion of steering.
